content:
iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo were released this week, and Apple has begun accepting iPhone Air and iPhone 17 as trade-ins for new purchases. However, the iPhone Air trade-in offer leaves a slightly bitter taste, especially after this week's price hike.

Apple usually waits until the new iPhone version launches before accepting older models for trade-in, but this time the iPhone Air and iPhone 17 are different — there is no iPhone Air 2 or iPhone 18 yet, and the earliest we might see these new models is early next year.

Nevertheless, Apple wants to give iPhone Air and iPhone 17 users a chance to upgrade to the iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone Duo, so these two models that Apple still sells can be used for trade-in.

As for the iPhone 17, after this week's $100 price increase, it now starts at $899, and Apple offers up to $585 in trade-in credit.

The iPhone Air also got a $100 price hike this week, with the starting price rising to $1,099. That's $200 more expensive than the iPhone 17 — so how much is the trade-in credit? Also $585. Honestly, speechless.

Apple's trade-in valuation table almost looks like a typo with an extra $100, but they are likely pricing based on demand and component value. Thinking about it more carefully, it's actually quite a pity, because the chip used in the iPhone Air is almost identical to the one in the iPhone 17 Pro.

To sum up, the iPhone Air is priced $100 higher for new customers, yet its trade-in value for existing customers — at least by Apple's calculation — is on par with a phone that is $200 cheaper. Not a great look.
